'''''Sisyrinchium montanum''''', the '''blue-eyed-grass''', '''American blue-eyed-grass''',<ref>{{GRIN | accessdate=1 July 2014}}</ref> or '''strict blue-eyed grass''',<ref>{{PLANTS |symbol=SIMOM |taxon=Sisyrinchium montanum var. montanum}}</ref> is a grass-like species of plant from the [[genus]] ''[[Sisyrinchium]]'', native to northern [[North America]] from [[Newfoundland (island)|Newfoundland]] west to easternmost [[Alaska]], and south to [[Pennsylvania]] in the east, and to [[New Mexico]] in the [[Rocky Mountains]]. It has also been introduced to parts of [[France]], likely during the [[First World War]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atlasobscura.com/articles/verdun-battle-wildlife-refuge|title=In France, a Bloody WWI Battlefield Has Become a Wildlife Refuge|author=Sabrina Imbler|publisher=Atlas Obscura|access-date= December 10, 2019|quote=Patches of the forest bloom with ''Sisyrinchium montanum'', or American blue-eyed grass, which stowed away as seeds on the hooves of U.S. Army horses that came through Verdun.|date=2019-12-06}}</ref>

It is very similar to ''[[Sisyrinchium angustifolium|S. angustifolium]]'', with which it is sometimes combined.<ref name=fna>{{eFloras|1|242101914|Sisyrinchium montanum |family=Iridaceae |first1=Anita F. |last1=Cholewa |first2=Douglass M. |last2=Henderson}}</ref>

==Description==
''Sisyrinchium montanum'' is a [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant]] that grows in clumps between {{convert|10|and|50|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} tall. Its [[plant stem|stem]]s have wings with entire to finely toothed margins. The [[leaf|leaves]] and stem are slender, {{convert|3|mm|in|frac=16|abbr=on}} broad, green or brownish, with sharp edges and a fine point.

The [[flower]]s are produced in a small [[Cyme (botany)|cyme]] of two to five together emerging from a [[spathe]], each flower about {{convert|2|cm|in|frac=4|abbr=on}} diameter, with six purplish [[tepal]]s with a yellowish base and yellow stamens. The [[fruit]] is a [[capsule (fruit)|capsule]] {{convert|4.5|–|6|mm|in|abbr=on}} long, containing numerous small black [[seed]]s.<ref name=fna/><ref name=bc>Plants of British Columbia: [http://linnet.geog.ubc.ca/Atlas/Atlas.aspx?sciname=Sisyrinchium+montanum ''Sisyrinchium montanum'']</ref>
